source.title: How Visual Representations Map to Language Feature Space in Multimodal LLMs
source.authors: Constantin Venhoff; Ashkan Khakzar; Sonia Joseph; P. Torr; Neel Nanda

record.tranche_reason: The study measures SAE reconstruction error to analyze visual-to-language representation alignment, but does not test linear predictability of SAE errors, error scaling across SAE sizes, or any other listed claim version.
record.gate_note: The paper reports layer-wise SAE reconstruction error for different token-position groups. These measurements concern SAE error, but do not test the defining properties in V1–V6. The plotted curves do not provide extractable numeric values. Benchmark scores and sparsity measurements are not results on the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The study uses pretrained GemmaScope SAE reconstruction error, sparsity and feature descriptions as a probe of visual-to-language alignment in a frozen-LLM VLM. It does not test linear predictability of the error (V1) or error scaling across SAE sizes (V2). It does not compare loss under spliced reconstructions against random errors (V3), decompose the error (V4), check circuits or steering with and without the error term (V5), or vary SAE training (V6). It does not cite the dark-matter paper. The SAE is a measuring tool here, so the study is T4 (uses_without_test), not T6 (discusses): it relies on SAE error as an instrument and reports only what that instrument shows about alignment.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that SAE reconstruction error, sparsity and semantic alignment converge around layer 18 of 26. They read this as visual representations being fully mapped onto LLM features there while remaining misaligned in earlier layers, which raises questions about adapter-based architectures.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses pretrained GemmaScope SAEs to measure reconstruction error across layers in a frozen multimodal model; it does not apply the dark-matter error-structure method described by the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Layer and token-position group: the paper reports layer-wise curves and distinguishes prompt, image, and image-text positions.

fits_no_version.finding: Layer-wise GemmaScope SAE MSE and sparsity for projected visual tokens fall and converge toward text-only levels around layer 18 of Gemma-2-2b-it. GPT-4o-judged semantic match of the features to image content rises at the same layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE reconstruction error on adapter-projected visual tokens in a frozen LLM decreases in middle-to-late layers, indicating alignment of those tokens with the language feature space.

record.problems: Only one language-model backbone is analyzed; the reported reconstruction-error values are presented in plots without extractable numerical values or stated uncertainty.

untested.parts: All of it: whether the error vector is linearly predictable from the input activation.
All of it: per-token error-norm predictability across SAE sizes, whether larger SAEs fail on the same contexts, and whether the error persists with scale.
All of it: loss under spliced-in SAE reconstructions compared with random errors of the same size.
All of it: splitting the error into linear and nonlinear parts and testing further dictionary learning on each.
All of it: whether feature-based circuits or steering lose behaviour when the error term is dropped.
All of it: whether SAE training choices or architecture drive the size of the error.

record.verdict_notes: The relation and tranche are changed from discusses/T6 to uses_without_test/T4, because the SAE error is the paper's instrument. The study has no bearing on any dark-matter version. The error here is measured on out-of-distribution visual inputs to an SAE trained on text activations, a different construct from intrinsic SAE dark matter.

versions.untested_parts: Whether a large share of the error vector is a linear function of the input activation.
Per-token error-norm predictability across SAE sizes, overlap in contexts where larger and smaller SAEs fail, and whether error persists with scale.
Whether SAE reconstruction harms model loss more than random errors of the same size.
Whether linear error contains unlearned features and nonlinear error resists further dictionary learning.
Whether omitting SAE error from feature-based analyses loses model behaviour.
Whether SAE training choices cause dark matter or whether improved architectures or end-to-end training reduce it.
